claim_one_line: THE MOVES: WHAT 'NO PERIOD' REMOVES AMONG THE GRAMMAR'S WORDS, AND THE STATUS OF EACH OF THE FOUR ITEMS (WP-1.3's first step; exact integer matrices, 11 checks, none failing). None of the four items is derived from the principle here: the unit shears (GM2) are declared; no period (GM3) is declared, as two clauses; reversible updates (GM5a) are declared; inverse moves (GM5b) are a reading adopted at version 1.48 by a ruling that a computation made. WHAT 'NO PERIOD' DOES: with the two shears alone no word has finite order (all 8,190 positive words of length at most 12; for every length, since such a product has non-negative entries and a diagonal of at least 1), the words that are not hyperbolic are exactly the words in one letter, and 'no period' removes none of them: what removes them is the clause that both letters occur, under which the trace is at least 3 and is 3 at LR and RL alone. With the inverse letters every trace from -2 to 2 occurs, the words of trace -1, 0 and 1 have orders 3, 4 and 6, and 'no period' removes exactly those; a single shear is the identity at no power and stays. This is the content, computed, of B1867's finding that the principle's formal statement removes finite order and not a fixed direction. NOT SHOWN: that the principle forces any of the four, or that both letters must occur. The foundation is not changed in this arc. 0 of 19.
